title: Ceramic Grinding Media — settlement submission of Merckaert Ceramic Media NV (Case AT.41786)
text:
RAVAILLÉ DEBLONDE
Avocats — Advocaten
Boulevard Bischoffsheim 27, 1000 Brussels
T +32 2 555 62 39
ravaille-deblonde.example.be

By hand and by secure e-mail

European Commission
Directorate-General for Competition
Place Madou 1, 1210 Brussels

Our ref: CRA/26/3428-MCM
Your ref: Case AT.41786
Brussels, 10 September 2026

STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL — SETTLEMENT SUBMISSION

Re: Case AT.41786 — Ceramic Grinding Media — Settlement submission of MERCKAERT CERAMIC MEDIA NV and ORVALLINE INDUSTRIES B.V. under Article 10a of Regulation (EC) No 773/2004

Dear Madam, Dear Sir,

1. We, Ravaillé Deblonde SRL (the "Firm"), act for Merckaert Ceramic Media NV, a Belgian public limited liability company with registered office at Ter Biest 44, 8790 Waregem, enterprise number 0682.315.402 (RLE Ghent, division Kortrijk) ("MCM"), and for its sole shareholder, Orvalline Industries B.V., a Dutch private limited liability company with registered office in Breda ("Orvalline" and, together with MCM, the "Parties").

2. Further to the settlement discussions between MCM and DG Competition on 17 March, 28 April and 9 June 2026, the Parties submit their settlement submission pursuant to Article 10a(2) of Regulation (EC) No 773/2004 and point 20 of the Commission Notice on the conduct of settlement procedures (the "Settlement Notice"), within the time limit set by the Commission's letter of 20 August 2026 under point 17 thereof.

I. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF LIABILITY

3. The Parties acknowledge, in clear and unequivocal terms, their liability for a single and continuous infringement of Article 101 TFEU and Article 53 of the EEA Agreement consisting in price coordination and customer allocation for zirconia grinding beads throughout the EEA (the "Infringement").

4. MCM participated in the Infringement from 3 February 2017 until 22 November 2023. Orvalline, which held 100% of MCM's share capital throughout, is liable as parent company for the same period.

5. The other participants, as identified by the case team, were Ziegelhoff Mahlkörper GmbH, Selb ("Ziegelhoff"), Perlati Microsfere S.r.l., Sassuolo ("Perlati"), and Fenwright Milling Media Ltd, Stoke-on-Trent ("Fenwright").

6. The contacts took place in the margins of the technical committee of the European Ceramic Media Federation ("ECMF"), a trade association seated in Maastricht, and outside the ECMF framework at the Hotel Marienbrunn in Nuremberg (8 March 2018, 21 June 2019 and 22 November 2023) and at the Villa Serramonte in Modena (15 October 2021).

7. For MCM, the contacts were conducted by Mr. Geert Blancquaert, Sales Director until the end of 2023, and Ms. Lieselot Deraedt, Key Account Manager Europe, without the knowledge of MCM's board. The Commission's file refers in particular to Dr. Ulrike Maschke, Managing Director of Ziegelhoff, who convened the Nuremberg meetings, Mr. Corrado Vezzani, Commercial Director of Perlati, and Ms. Harriet Pollington, Sales Director of Fenwright. [1]

[1] See the message of 12 October 2021 quoted at paragraph 148 of the summary of objections: "Vezzani will circulate the revised list before Modena; Blancquaert to confirm the Benelux surcharge by Friday."

8. The Parties accept the facts, their legal qualification and MCM's role and duration of participation as presented in the summary of objections of 2 July 2026. MCM acted as a follower: Dr. Maschke and Mr. Vezzani, not Mr. Blancquaert or Ms. Deraedt, set the agenda of the meetings in paragraph 6.

II. MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF THE FINE

9. The Parties have been informed of the range of likely fines under the 2006 Guidelines on the method of setting fines (the "Fining Guidelines"), including a 25% reduction for MCM as second applicant under point 26 of the Commission Notice on Immunity from fines and reduction of fines in cartel cases (the "Leniency Notice") and the 10% reduction under point 32 of the Settlement Notice.

10. The Parties accept that the Commission may impose on them, jointly and severally, a fine not exceeding EUR 23,650,000 (the "Maximum Fine"), which does not exceed 10% of Orvalline's consolidated turnover for 2025 within the meaning of Article 23(2) of Regulation (EC) No 1/2003.

III. PROCEDURAL CONFIRMATIONS

11. The Parties confirm that (a) they have been sufficiently informed of the objections the Commission intends to raise against them and have had sufficient opportunity to make their views known; (b) they do not envisage requesting access to the file or an oral hearing before the Hearing Officer, unless the statement of objections or the decision does not reflect this submission; and (c) they agree to receive the statement of objections and the final decision in English.

12. In that event the acknowledgements above shall be deemed withdrawn under points 27 and 29 of the Settlement Notice. This submission is without prejudice to the Parties' right of action before the General Court under Article 263 TFEU; no copy should be made available to Ziegelhoff, Perlati or Fenwright other than under Article 15(1a) of Regulation (EC) No 773/2004 and Article 6(6) of Directive 2014/104/EU.

13. Correspondence should be addressed to the undersigned, Ms. Céline Ravaillé (c.ravaille@ravaille-deblonde.example.be, +32 2 555 62 39), with a copy to Mr. Wouter Nyssens of this Firm (w.nyssens@ravaille-deblonde.example.be, +32 473 91 08 55). MCM's General Counsel, Mr. Bavo Casier, and Orvalline's managing director, Ms. Maud Lejoncourt, should be contacted through the Firm only.

Yours faithfully,

Céline Ravaillé
Partner
Ravaillé Deblonde SRL
Counsel for the Parties

Enclosures: powers of attorney signed by Mr. Casier (MCM) and Ms. Lejoncourt (Orvalline).

cc: Mr. Bavo Casier, General Counsel, MCM (by secure e-mail)
